Let $\pi_i(v)$ denote the projected pixel location.
**Surface Extraction (Coarse):** For an arbitrary 3D location $q$, apply positional encoding $\operatorname{PE}$ to its 3D coordinates.
Interpolate the features from the coarse geometry encoding volume $M_{\text{coarse}}(q)$.
**Surface Extraction (Fine):** Use the coarse geometry to guide the fine level.
Interpolate features from the fine geometry encoding volume $M_{\text{fine}}(q)$ (which is constructed similarly to $M_{\text{coarse}}$ but at higher resolution).
**Color Blending:** Use a multi-scale color blending module to predict colors by aggregating information from the input images.
**Consistency-Aware Loss:** Introduce a consistency-aware fine-tuning scheme to control inconsistent regions caused by occlusion and noise.
**Optimization:** Optimize the model using the same $N$ input images without adding new images.
**SDF Rescaling:** Use a hyperparameter $\tau$ to rescale the SDF value of sampled points behind visible surfaces.
*   **Radiance Ambiguity:** With sparse views (e.g., 3 images), radiance ambiguity can cause distorted and incomplete geometry in methods like [NeuS](6060-neus.md) and [MVSNerf](9325-hame-nerf.md).
*   **Weak Textures:** Conventional MVS methods like COLMAP fail with weak textures.
*   **Background Noise:** DTU dataset images contain large black backgrounds with considerable noise.
*   **Time Complexity:** The generic model training involves two stages of 150k iterations each.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Uses sparse 3D CNNs with resolutions $96 \times 96 \times 96$ and $192 \times 192 \times 192$.
*   **When to Use:** When only sparse multi-view images are available and generalization to new scenes is required.
*   **When Not to Use:** When dense views are available and per-scene optimization is acceptable (e.g., [NeuS](6060-neus.md) might be simpler).
